en: The *Jñānolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaprabha and others by imperial decree during the Tang dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling within the Palace of the Sun and Moon, together with immeasurable great bodhisattvas.
Together with the assembly of bodhisattvas were Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
Dhāraṇīśvararāja Bodhisattva, and Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
With such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as their leaders,
at that time there was a Buddha in the eastern direction named Jñānolkā Tathāgata,
and in the southern direction there was a Buddha.
He is named Tathāgata Golden Light Cluster.
In the western direction there is a Buddha named Tathāgata Truth-Speaker.
In the northern direction there is a Buddha named Tathāgata King of Thunderous Sound.
Each had come from their own country to this assembly.
At that time, the World-Honored One, together with the assembly of Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas,
was all within the Golden Banner Pavilion.
Each sat upon a lion throne adorned with jewels.
At that time, the Sun and Moon Devas came to where the Buddha was,
prostrating themselves with their heads at the feet of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in reverent salutation.
They made offerings with various exquisite objects.
Having completed the offerings, they withdrew to sit on one side and said to one another:
How have we obtained from the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas this *dhāraṇī* of the Torch of Wisdom that Fills the Ten Directions, which emanates light for all sentient beings and shatters all darkness?
"By the power of this dhāraṇī,
may we be able to act as great luminous torches for the sake of sentient beings.
When these words were spoken,
Those Tathāgatas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas then spoke this mantra with one voice: *Svāhā*. (Note:
Regarding the pronunciation of this character, the upper radical is pronounced with the third tone [細], while the lower part has a phonetic note indicating the first tone [上].)
All follow this pattern: *yathā* (1), *cakra* (2), *cakrapravarta* (3),
*duramita* (4), *kākarudra* (5), *itastataḥ*.

The "fan" (反) in the following [syllables] is the same; the "sa" (娑) at the beginning of the sixth phrase is pronounced with a retroflex tongue-sound based on the original phonetic value of the character *sū* (蘇).

Within this mantra, whenever there is a sound like *lū*, *li*, *lu*, or *lā* produced from the mouth, they are all to be treated in this manner. The "ṭa" (吒) at the end of the seventh phrase is pronounced as *du-jiǎ* (都假);
the "su" (蘇) at the beginning of the eighth phrase is *tā* (拕); the "su" (蘇) at the beginning of the ninth phrase is *tā* (哆), with the "ding-zuǒ" (丁佐) tone; the final syllable is *i-tán-sā* (壹炭娑).

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the gods of the sun and moon.
The Son of the Buddha said:
"O sons of the gods, this dhāraṇī was expounded by eighty-eight billion Buddhas,
Tathāgatas, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings."
"O sons of the gods, while the udumbara flower may still appear with relative ease,
the manifestation of this dhāraṇī is exceedingly difficult.
O sons of the gods, while one may still encounter the appearance of Buddhas in the world,"
This dhāraṇī is extremely difficult to encounter;
yet this dhāraṇī may still be easily obtained.
For those who recite and uphold it,
this is even more difficult to achieve.
O sons of the gods, if you wish to rescue and deliver those who have committed the five heinous crimes or who slander those who uphold the True Dharma, [you must do so through this].
Those who are to undergo the sufferings of the Avīci Hell should,
in a secluded place, cleanse and smear the ground with pure substances and make offerings of various kinds of incense and flowers as they can afford.
During the twenty-one days, at the six periods of day and night,
one shall recite this dhāraṇī mantra.
By the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī, [the following occurs].
It shall cause the Avīci Hell to be destroyed at that very moment into hundreds of thousands of fragments,
and the sentient beings therein shall immediately attain liberation;
how much more so for those who, while dwelling among humans, are able to hear it?
You should know that such a person is protected and sustained by the Buddhas, as well as by us Bodhisattvas.
O sons of the gods, do not give rise to doubt regarding what has been said here.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the assembly of devas of the sun and moon rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra of the Wisdom-Torch Dhāraṇī.
